title: Can a 15 cm square handkerchief be cut from a cloth of area 125?
description: The area needed for a handkerchief of side fifteen centimetres is found and compared with the area of the cloth. Then the cloth's area is placed between two squares to find the largest whole number side. Keeko doubts the first comparison, because fifteen is less than one hundred twenty five.
teaching_notes: One idea: compare areas with areas, and find the side by placing the area between two squares. Watch for students who compare a side in centimetres with an area in square centimetres.

source: Akhil's square cloth has area 125 cm². Can he cut a square h
video_script.why: The child uses squares around an area to decide what whole number side a square can have.
video_script.substitution: Find the area a side needs, compare it with the area available, then place the area between two squares.
video_script.anchor: a square piece of cloth of area one hundred twenty five square centimetres
video_script.wrong_answer: fifteen is less than one hundred twenty five
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko compares the side fifteen with the area one hundred twenty five and says the handkerchief fits. A side and an area cannot be compared; the handkerchief needs an area of two hundred twenty five.
video_script.payoff_line: No, the largest whole number side is eleven centimetres

final_answer.value: No; the largest whole number side is 11 cm
final_answer.spoken: no, the largest whole number side is eleven centimetres

Eleven squared is one hundred twenty one, and twelve squared is one hundred forty four.
<bookmark mark='between'/>One hundred twenty five sits between them. The side of the cloth is between eleven and twelve centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks fifteen is less than one hundred twenty five, so the handkerchief fits.
<bookmark mark='kinds'/>But fifteen is a side in centimetres, and one hundred twenty five is an area in square centimetres.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Only an area can be compared with an area.
